text:
Aisha (CS): quick thread — putting together a customer-facing 'warmup syncpoint' playbook for onboarding accounts that rely heavily on streaming + prefill. want feedback before i share with the field.

Leo (Solutions): love the name. main goals? reduce cold-start latency, capture signals for renewal-risk, and keep customers in control of cost, right? :100:

Aisha (CS): exactly. also need a short telemetry checklist so SRE/product can surface account health in the console. thinking of 3 checkpoints: prefill success rate, first-10-min latency P95, streaming connection failure rate.

Ravi (SRE): agree. add kv-cache hit ratio and prefix-cache eviction spikes. those tell us if their model/sequence strategy is wrong.

Marta (Customer): from our side, we need simple instructions customers can follow during the kickoff call. like a one-minute checklist we can run together.

Aisha (CS): draft one-minute customer checklist (for kickoff):
• Confirm steady traffic pattern sample (5–10 requests/min)
• Run a 5-min prefill with real prompts (prefill size 50–200 tokens)
• Observe streaming handshake and token arrival times
• Verify CSP/network egress rules for streaming websocket

Leo (Solutions): add a short config snippet customers can paste for prefill TTL and batching hints.

Aisha (CS): good call — sample:```
# recommended defaults for initial onboarding
redwood.prefill.enable = true
redwood.prefill.size = 100
redwood.prefill.ttl = 600  # seconds
redwood.batch.max_concurrent = 8
redwood.streaming.keepalive = 30  # seconds
```

Ravi (SRE): for internal telemetry mapping, propose these event keys: `prefill.start`, `prefill.finish`, `stream.open`, `stream.error`, `cache.hit`, `cache.eviction`, `latency.p95`. tie them to customer health scoring.

Aisha (CS): nice. how should CS capture renewal-risk flags during kickoff? short verbatim script?

Marta (Customer): yes — we ask two direct questions during handshake: 1) "How critical is response latency to this feature?" 2) "Are there compliance/network constraints we should know now?" If answer to Q1 is "very", escalate to Dedicated capacity playbook.

Leo (Solutions): escalate flow: if p95 > 600ms on baseline prefill or streaming error rate > 2% -> create a dedicated runbook ticket and loop infra/solutions.

Aisha (CS): also include a lightweight troubleshooting checklist for customers that admins can run without IR help:
• Check websocket health: `wscat -c wss://api.redwood.ai/stream`
• Inspect prefill logs in console -> filter `prefill.*` events
• Toggle prefill off to test on-demand latency

Ravi (SRE): pro tip: if cache.eviction spikes after rollout, recommend increasing prefill.ttl incrementally (600 -> 1200) and bump batch.max_concurrent down one step while monitoring CPU/GPU utilization.

onboard-bot: onboarding-docs: created draft at https://redwood.internal/docs/cs/warmup-syncpoint-playbook (preview link) :file_folder:

Aisha (CS): final section — feedback capture template for CS handoff: 3 bullets to collect post-kickoff (24–72h):
1) actual avg QPS and latency after 24h
2) any streaming disconnect occurrences with timestamps
3) qualitative customer sentiment ("latency fine / borderline / unacceptable")

Marta (Customer): we'll start using that template in our next 3 kickoff calls, will report back with any wording tweaks.

Leo (Solutions): i'll add a small visual to the doc showing where the telemetry maps into the account health dashboard (prefill success, cache hit, stream errors).

Aisha (CS): thank you all — i'll polish and post the customer-facing checklist + the internal telemetry mapping. leaving this thread open for any quick edits. :sparkles:
